newsitem.title: USA: Office Depot net rises, but merger costs take toll.
newsitem.headline: Office Depot net rises, but merger costs take toll.

text.p: Office supply retailer Office Depot Inc. reported earnings growth of 8 percent for the second quarter, but costs tied to its unsuccessful effort to merge with Staples Inc. cut into profits, the company said Thursday.
Office Depot said its second-quarter net income climbed to $30.5 million, or 19 cents a share, from $28.3 million, or 18 cents a share a year ago.
The second-quarter results included a charge of $9.5 million related to its failed bid to merge with Westborough, Mass.-based Staples.
The two companies had announced the merger pact last September, but the deal was scrapped nine months later after federal regulators ruled against it on antitrust grounds.
Total sales for Delray Beach, Fla.-based Office Depot rose 11 percent in the second quarter, to $1.53 billion from $1.38 billion a year ago.
Office Depot said the merger efforts cost the company $16.1 million for the six-month period ended June 28, 1997.
Separately, the company said Thursday it plans to open approximately 40 new stores in 1997 and at least 80 stores in 1998.

Office Depot operates 575 stores and 23 delivery centres in the United States and Canada, making it the nation's second biggest office products supplier after Staples. The company also has 32 stores outside the United States and Canada, including 10 in Mexico and eight in Israel.
Office Depot rose 50 cents to $17.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
